analyticalQuestion: Does retaining the common input slope x=s/j across the complete positive large-charge column remove enough of the R0.43 termwise-maximization loss to close the reduced canonical restart at r=37/100, and which sector becomes the next bottleneck?
supportedClaim: For every large positive input charge s>=241 and every admissible tail degree j>80, positive domination reduces the complete center column to H_r(x)=sum |a_iq| r^i d_i beta_q |i*x-q|/3 on the shared interval 0<=x<=2. Because H_r is convex, its all-order maximum is attained at x=0 or x=2. At r=37/100 the two endpoints are 0.56025596671784847152 and 0.96621300575693572712, the complete active-tail bound is 0.99701184124819861673, and all fixed-point and canonical-stretch gates pass. At r=371/1000 the large sector remains below one but the inherited finite s=-1 sufficient column reaches 1.0008564924160487608, identifying the next proof bottleneck.
